\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\sphinxAtStartPar
This manual is organized around how users actually consume the layer:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
start with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{quickstart}} for the short\sphinxhyphen{}path workflow

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {}

\section{Include Path}
\label{\detokenize{quickstart:include-path}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}platform}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{pCPU}\PYG{p}{)}

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample\_like(...)}} preserves the visible tensor contract from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{like}}: shape, dtype, and platform. \section{Intended Style}
\label{\detokenize{quickstart:intended-style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The user\sphinxhyphen{}facing model is:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keep everything under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::distr}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
pass the distribution name plus a short parameter list

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
use typed wrappers like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::distr::Normal}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bernoulli}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Binomial}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Gamma}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Uniform}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Exponential}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Skellam}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nig}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GaussianMixture}} when a bound object is clearer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
let \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample\_like}} carry shape and dtype when you already have a target tensor

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
stay on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} throughout instead of bouncing between helper wrappers

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope


\chapter{API Reference}

\chapter{Object API Reference}
\label{\detokenize{object_api_reference:object-api-reference}}\label{\detokenize{object_api_reference::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The object wrappers bind distribution parameters once, then expose a method surface that stays on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} throughout:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample(...)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample\_like(...)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pdf(...)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{logpdf(...)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cdf(...)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{logcdf(...)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cgf(...)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumulant(...)}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use them when the distribution itself is part of the model state and repeated calls should not keep re\sphinxhyphen{}spelling the parameter list.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Output}} blocks below were verified from the compiled demo \DUrole{xref}{\DUrole{download}{\DUrole{myst}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{distributions\_objects\_demo.cpp}}}}} using the fixed seed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20260303ULL}} on CPU. If you change dtype, platform, or seed, sampled values will change.

\label{\detokenize{object_api_reference:id5}}

\subsection{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{object_api_reference:id26}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Stores the normal parameters in log\sphinxhyphen{}space and evaluates on the positive real line. The CGF is only documented on the nonpositive grid used in the demo because the ordinary moment generating function diverges for positive arguments.

\subsection{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{object_api_reference:id29}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Represents a bounded continuous law on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}low, high{]}}}. Higher\sphinxhyphen{}order cumulants come from the interval raw moments, so the object remains useful beyond simple sampling.

\subsection{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{object_api_reference:id68}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Wraps a Gaussian mixture with component weights, means, and standard deviations stored as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}. The wrapper validates component\sphinxhyphen{}shape compatibility and supports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{use\_sobol=true}} for Sobol\sphinxhyphen{}driven sampling.

\subsection{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{distribution_catalog:id14}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Discrete non\sphinxhyphen{}negative count family normalized by the modified Bessel function \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{I\_nu(a)}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nu}} must stay above \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a}} must be positive. This is the right model when the count law itself is defined through a Bessel\sphinxhyphen{}function normalization rather than through a Poisson or negative\sphinxhyphen{}binomial construction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Aliases: none.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Parameters: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{nu, a\}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample\_like(...)}} when you want the sampled output to inherit shape, dtype, and platform from an existing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}.

\subsection{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{distribution_catalog:id95}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Discrete positive\sphinxhyphen{}count family with exponentially damped tails. Use it when you want a count distribution that stays strictly positive and decays faster than a pure power law. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lambda}} sets the near\sphinxhyphen{}origin shape and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scale}} controls the tail decay rate.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Aliases: none.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Parameters: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{lambda, scale\}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample\_like(...)}} when you want the sampled output to inherit shape, dtype, and platform from an existing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}.

\subsection{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{distribution_catalog:id152}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Generalized inverse Gaussian family on the positive real line. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lambda}} selects the subfamily, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chi}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{psi}} control the inverse\sphinxhyphen{}Gaussian versus gamma\sphinxhyphen{}like pull on the tails. In practice this is the workhorse mixing law behind several heavier\sphinxhyphen{}tailed continuous models, including the generalized hyperbolic family.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Aliases: none.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Parameters: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{lambda, chi, psi\}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample\_like(...)}} when you want the sampled output to inherit shape, dtype, and platform from an existing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}.

\subsection{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{distribution_catalog:id155}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Five\sphinxhyphen{}parameter generalized hyperbolic family for skewed, heavy\sphinxhyphen{}tailed continuous data. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lambda}} chooses the subclass, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{beta}} control tail weight and asymmetry, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mu}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{delta}} provide location and scale. This is the flexible parent family behind special cases like NIG.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Aliases: none.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Parameters: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{lambda, alpha, beta, mu, delta\}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample\_like(...)}} when you want the sampled output to inherit shape, dtype, and platform from an existing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}.

\subsection{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{distribution_catalog:id158}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Normal\sphinxhyphen{}inverse\sphinxhyphen{}Gaussian special case of the generalized hyperbolic family, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{alpha \textgreater{} |beta|}} required by the runtime. Use it when you need a continuous law that can stay much more tail\sphinxhyphen{}heavy and skewed than a Gaussian while still supporting direct sampling, density evaluation, and object\sphinxhyphen{}based cumulant generation through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::distr::Nig}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Aliases: none.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Parameters: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{alpha, beta, mu, delta\}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample\_like(...)}} when you want the sampled output to inherit shape, dtype, and platform from an existing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}.
